$description: Editorial & print: warm stone paper, Fraunces display serif paired with Plus Jakarta Sans, 1px hairline rules, flat cards, and crimson + cobalt inks.

color.$description: Warm paper and warm charcoal, one red ink and one press blue. The neutrals carry the weight; the red is the spot colour, spent on marks and on the destructive action, never on a large surface.

primary.$description: The brand's red. An ordinary action wears the brand, and the destructive action wears a hotter vermilion, so the two never read as one intent.

secondary.$description: The quiet fill: paper one step off the page, for a control that is present but not asking for attention.

neutral.$description: The paper ramp: warm at every step, and the same ten steps restated for the night press, so a mode is a change of ink rather than a change of system.

semantic.$description: Status colours, named by meaning. The red is both the accent and the destructive ink, so a danger and a mark are the same word on purpose; the rest are quiet enough to sit beside it.

success.$description: A low, warm green: the colour of a thing that worked, kept dark enough never to compete with the ink.

warning.$description: A printer's ochre: a mark that asks to be read before it is acted on.

error.$description: The alarm: a hotter vermilion beside the brand's crimson. Two reds, the way a print shop runs a second colour beside a spot — and the destructive action can never be mistaken for the ordinary one.

info.$description: The press blue, the same ink as the link: information is a link that is not yet a link.

surface.$description: The page. Warm paper in the day; after dark the night's charcoal, which is a paper of its own rather than the absence of one.

surface-sunken.$description: A surface that sits below the page: table stripes, inset wells, the trough a field is carved into.

surface-raised.$description: A surface that sits above the page: cards, popovers, menus. Pure white on the paper page, and one clean step up the charcoal ramp after dark.

text.$description: Body text: ink on paper, paper on ink.

text-muted.$description: The second voice: captions, helper copy, the small print that still has to be read.

border.$description: The hairline. Spin draws in thread: a one-pixel rule is what separates one thing from the next, so there are fewer boxes here than in a theme that leans on shadow.

scrim.$description: What dims the page behind a modal: the theme's own ink, laid over the sheet.

on-primary.$description: The ink on the brand red: paper in the day, and the red's own near-black on the night press.

focus-ring.$description: The press blue, and only the press blue: the ring never wears a colour that means something else.

link.$description: The press blue. A link in running text is blue and never the red, so a link and a danger are never the same word on a page.

on-secondary.$description: The ink on the quiet fill: the deepest ink in the ramp, in either mode.

on-semantic-success.$description: The ink on the success fill.

on-semantic-warning.$description: The ink on the warning fill.

field.$description: A field's own surface: a lifted step off the page, so a control reads as an object set on the sheet rather than a hole punched through it.

border-strong.$description: A control's own edge — the thread drawn a shade tighter, for a field or a switch that must read as an object. It is the one rule a finger has to find, so it carries enough weight to be seen: three to one against the page, or the control is not a control.

on-semantic-error.$description: The ink on the error fill. A fill with no readable foreground cannot be read, which is what this token prevents.

on-danger.$description: The legacy name for the ink on the error fill. It points at `color.on-semantic-error` — the role the contract requires, the floor is measured on, and the danger button and the danger badge wear — so the two names can never disagree.

on-semantic-info.$description: The ink on the info fill.

disabled.$description: The fill a dead control wears: one step off the paper, in the ramp's own warm grey. A control that cannot be pressed is still printed — it is simply printed in the quiet ink.

on-disabled.$description: The ink on that fill: the second voice, the one the small print is set in. Dimming the control would dim this with it, and the label is the one thing a dead control still has to say.

32.$description: The macro gap: the air between two sections of a page, which is where this theme puts its emphasis instead of putting a box around them.

spacing.$description: The spacing scale. Every gap, pad and inset is one of these steps, and the roomiest step is the one that separates sections.

font.$description: One UI family, used with conviction, and one didone for the moments that are allowed to be a poster. Hierarchy is weight and size; no second typeface is spent on it.

sans.$value: Plus Jakarta Sans, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif
sans.$description: The working voice: quiet, even, and everywhere a tool has to be read.

heading.$description: The display voice: an expressive, ink-trapped technical grotesque with architectural poise.

body.$description: The body face: the sans under another name, so the surface reads whole.

serif.$description: Long-form editorial text. The didone is too sharp to read for pages, so the book serif takes the long reads.

mono.$value: JetBrains Mono, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, ui-monospace, monospace
mono.$description: Code, identifiers, tabular figures: the one face that is never wrong, because it never varies.

brand.$value: Bricolage Grotesque, Space Grotesk, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif
brand.$description: The logotype face — one brand, every language.

2xs.$description: The printed caption: small, set in caps and tracked open, the label above a field.

xl.$description: A section head, sized to be found rather than to be impressed.

2xl.$description: The head of a section that has to carry a column on its own.

3xl.$description: A page's own head, set in the didone at reading size.

display.$description: The poster. Three and three-quarter times the body, and the one step where the jump is a scale rather than a font size.

size.$description: Nine steps, and a jump at the top that is a scale rather than a size: a didone is measured in headlines, and the poster only gets one.

tracking.$description: How far the letters sit from each other. A didone is spaced open where the hairlines need air and closed nowhere.

display.$description: Display — the largest statement on the page. Hero headings (h1 reads it). Not section titles (that's title).

title.$description: Title — the section title. h2 and stat figures read it. Not subsections (that's heading).

heading.$description: Heading — the subsection title. h3 reads it. Not UI labels (that's label).

subtitle.$description: Subtitle — the large UI step. Large buttons (button s-lg falls back to it). Not intro paragraphs (that's lead).

lead.$description: Lead — the intro paragraph. Article ledes and empty-state subheads. Not default reading text (that's body).

body.$description: Body — the default reading text. Every paragraph. Not UI labels (that's label), not emphasis (that's body-emphasized).

quote.$description: Quote — somebody else's words (blockquote reads it). Not default reading text (that's body).

code.$description: Code — identifiers and paths (code reads it). Monospace. Not prose of any kind.

label.$description: Label — the short named thing. Field labels, card headers, badges (badge falls back to it). Not annotations (that's caption).

caption.$description: Caption — the annotation. Timestamps, helper text, stat context. Not named emphasis (that's caption-emphasized).

overline.$description: Overline — the kicker above a title (h5/h6 read it). Tracked out. Not a label (that's label).

body-emphasized.$description: Body, emphasized — definition terms (dt reads it). Same tuple as body except the semibold step. Not a second family (see the variant convention).

caption-emphasized.$description: Caption, emphasized — figcaptions and table headers (figcaption, th read it). Same tuple as caption except the semibold step.

radius.$description: Square geometry. A thread ends blunt: the poster has no round corners except where a control is a pill.

shadow.$description: Flat, and then one hard cut. A card is paper on paper, separated by a hairline and by air; only an overlay is cut out of the sheet, and it is cut with a hard unblurred offset. No blur anywhere in this theme.

lg.$description: The cut-out: a hard offset with no blur, the look of a sheet laid on the page. Only the overlays spend it.

motion.$description: Precise, and quick. Motion points; it does not perform — no overshoot, no bounce, and no loop that could read as a strobe.

fast.$description: A state change the reader has already decided to expect: a hover, a press, a focus.

base.$description: The default: a colour or a rule moving to its next position.

slow.$description: The longest a transition may take: a panel arriving, a drawer settling.

loop.$description: The period of an endless animation: the skeleton's pulse and the loop utilities. Slow enough to be watched rather than to be noticed.

button.$description: Component tokens: the decisions a theme owns for its buttons. Spin's button is a printed caption on a block of ink — uppercase, tracked open, flat at rest, and lifted by a hard two pixels when it is touched.

shadow.$description: Nothing at rest. The block is printed on the page; a shadow would make it a photograph of a block.

shadow-hover.$description: A hard two-pixel offset, the sheet lifting off the page by the width of a rule. No blur, no glow — the button is drawn, not lit.

badge.$description: Component tokens: the decisions a theme owns for its badges. Spin's badge is a square tag with an edge drawn like thread — no pills.

pill.$description: A pill is a soft word. Spin squares its badges into tags.

checkbox.$description: How physical a checkbox is: one scalar driving three inset shadows. Zero is flat and drawn — spin's controls are drawn, not lit.

padding.$description: The air inside the card, between its parts and around its edge.

elevation.$description: No elevation at all. A card is paper on paper, separated by a hairline and by air, and a shadow would make it a photograph of a sheet.
